title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
subtitle: Why quantum computers threaten RSA/ECC and what comes next

content.text: Shor's algorithm running on a large enough quantum computer can break RSA and ECC in polynomial time. NIST standardised new post-quantum algorithms in 2024.

content.definition: NIST-standardised key encapsulation mechanism resistant to quantum attacks.
NIST-standardised digital signature algorithm resistant to quantum attacks.

content.code:
Current algorithms and status:
  RSA-2048     — quantum-vulnerable (Shor's algorithm)
  ECDSA P-256  — quantum-vulnerable (Shor's algorithm)
  AES-256      — quantum-safe (Grover's halves effective key size; AES-256 still safe)
  SHA-256      — quantum-safe (need SHA-384+ for long-term)

NIST PQC Standards (2024):
  ML-KEM  (CRYSTALS-Kyber)    — key encapsulation
  ML-DSA  (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) — digital signatures
  SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+)          — hash-based signatures

content.text: Start planning a migration to post-quantum algorithms now. TLS 1.3 already supports hybrid ECDH+Kyber in Chrome and Cloudflare.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT threatened by Shor's algorithm?
questions.explanation: AES is a symmetric algorithm. Grover's algorithm halves its effective key size, but AES-256 retains ~128-bit quantum security — still safe.

faq.q: Should I migrate to post-quantum cryptography today?
faq.a: Begin inventory and planning now. For most apps, there is no urgency today. Prioritise long-lived secrets (keys, certificates) that protect data you need to keep private for 10+ years.
